call_points.text: MINPRO JV with Khemka: ₹35 Cr initial investment over two years, production targeted for Q4FY27.
Quartzite mines Chiraipani and Bhikampali expected to open by end of this quarter, with cost benefits from next quarter.
No project orders in Q1; glass and silica projects expected in Q3 and Q4, coke oven project at final negotiation.
Steel sector capex estimated at not less than ₹50,000-60,000 Cr this financial year, supporting refractory demand.
Magnesite prices rose 6-8% in the last two months; management is working to absorb or pass on the increase.
Alumina prices stable over the last six months, with no significant movement.
Cash and cash equivalents of ₹452 Cr; balance sheet net cash positive.
Exports declined from last quarter to this quarter; management expects flow control exports to rise over the coming months.
Auditor resigned mid-year to align with the parent group's auditor change; same auditors to be adopted at the upcoming AGM.
Five more coke oven batteries expected in 2-3 years; company conservatively expects at least two.
Seeking 1-3% price increases depending on segment, effective from May, to offset input cost rises.
High-cost fused magnesia and DBM inventory hit Feb and March shipments; alumina inventory is now at market pricing.
Goodwill impairment on RHIM IR (Dalmia assets) due to weaker exports, currency depreciation and new competitor capacity.
Dalmia assets revenue grew 14% to ₹1,153 Cr in FY26, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.8% from 11.5%.
Cement share of revenue fell to 11% from 13% as competition added capacity and filled plants at any cost.
Management declined to quantify the fixed-cost impact of iron making on quarterly numbers.
